title: Tic Tac Toe Showdown: Turn-Based Line-Matching Game
subtitle: A deep dive into the turn-based mechanics of Tic Tac Toe Showdown, covering alternating moves, line detection, and 3x3 grid win conditions. Readers will master exhaustive first-player strategies within a finite state space, implement line-matching logic through core loops and modular design, and configure key grid parameters.

cover.alt: Tic Tac Toe Showdown: Turn-Based Line-Matching Game

corePoints: 3x3 Board: Finite State Space, Exhaustive First-Player Strategies

breakdown.title: Game Objective
bullets: Connect your pieces into a line of the specified length first

breakdown.title: Core Loop
bullets: State Flow: boot → menu → gameplay → result; Core Actions: Alternating Turns + Piece Placement + Line Matching + Score Comparison + Decision Making
Your Task: Take turns with an opponent to place pieces on the grid, aiming to align identical pieces in a row.

breakdown.title: Module Composition
bullets: common-ui: Generic UI Event Binding Module: Automatically binds click events to button nodes in the skin and supports auto-transition from the boot scene to the menu.
core/board-turn: Generic Turn-Based Board Core: Manages grid board state, piece placement, and win detection (line/chain). Suitable for Tic Tac Toe, Gomoku, Four-in-a-Row, and simplified Go.
core/board-ai: Generic Board AI: Provides move decisions for board-turn. Current implementation uses minimax, supporting small-scale zero-sum games like Tic Tac Toe.
